attestations.text: CHANG Jan 張然 (T. 陶庵) 17th century, a native of Hsiu-shui, Chekiang, was the second son of Chang Lien [q. v.]. Adept at drawing and having learned landscape architecture from his father, he went to Peking and there constructed for Fêng P'u [q. v.] the garden known as Wan-liu-t'ang 萬柳堂, and for Wang Hsi [q. v.] the I-yüan 怡園, both famous private gardens much applauded by contemporary and later poets.
